policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders 'thy cities shall not be inhabited' (yashab), which is the ketiv תישבנה; the mapped textual_variant note 'Another reading is, return' relegates the qere תָשֹׁבְנָה (shub, 'return') to the margin, so the ASV text follows the ketiv.

ASV renders the plural 'They are laid desolate', matching the qere plural שָׁמֵמוּ; the singular ketiv שממה ('it is desolate') is carried only by the marginal 'Or, It is', which is classed alternative_rendering and does not itself decide, while the text's plural wording does.
